label: Input phase from the 3rd token through <DEL> (positional, encoding phase)
explanation: Positional/phase feature: active on input steps t >= 2 of the original phase and on the <DEL> step, essentially silent at t = 0-1 and throughout the copy phase (0.4% rate, 0.1% of mass). The firing rate per original position rises from 0.65 at t=2 to about 0.9 at orig_idx 7-8, and <DEL> fires 74% of the time (17% of mass). Activation mass is concentrated at t = 3-6. Magnitude depends on sequence content: the strongest examples start with a/w/t (first_tok a carries the most mass) and keep their peak around steps 3-5. Repeated tokens (in_first = 0) fire less often (rate 0.08 vs 0.56), but adding that condition lowers recall more than it raises precision. About 23% of predicted steps are inactive, mostly in sequences that are weak overall.

issues: The positional claims hold. Test scores for (t>=2)&(phase<=1) reproduce exactly: P 0.772, R 0.977, F1 0.862. Copy-phase rate is 0.4% with 0.1% of mass, <DEL> fires 74%, and t=0 never fires.

The false positives follow a pattern. Precision of the predicate depends strongly on the FIRST original token. With orig(0)=h it is 0.09; with e 0.34, f 0.30 and '1' 0.31. With j, x, z, u and n it is about 0.5-0.64. For most other first tokens (a, d, g, i, k-t, w) it is 0.95-1.0. So sequences that begin with h/e/f/1 largely suppress the feature for the whole encoding phase. The explanation calls the 23% inactive predicted steps 'sequences that are weak overall' but never names this cause.
Related h/1 effect: any step where h or 1 has already been seen has precision 0.58 (vs 0.84 when not seen). With h/1 at orig(0), precision is 0.20.

The misses also follow a pattern. At t=1 the feature fires whenever in_tok is h or 1: (t==1)&isin(in_tok,[h,1]) has precision 1.0 and accounts for most of the t=1 activity. Within t>=2, h/1 inputs fire with precision 0.94. These tokens fire the feature themselves but suppress it later on.

The repeated-token claim is misleading. The quoted 'rate 0.08 vs 0.56' mixes in copy-phase steps. Within the encoding phase (t>=2, phase 0), repeated tokens (in_first=0) fire MORE often (precision 0.84) than first occurrences (0.77).

Minor point: the label 'from the 3rd token' is fine, but the explanation's statement that magnitude is driven by a/w/t first tokens only gives the high end. The more informative content effect is the strong suppression by a few first tokens.
skeptic.revised_label: Encoding-phase feature (t>=2 through <DEL>), suppressed in sequences that start with h/e/f/1; fires on h/1 inputs from t=1

final_label: Encoding-phase feature (t>=2 through <DEL>), suppressed in sequences that start with h/e/f/1; fires on h/1 inputs from t=1

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: w, a, t, s, d, k; least: e, f, 1, h) and the current input token, by step (t=1: 1, h, z; t=2: h, 1, z, f; t=11: a, l, t, w); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=4, t=6.
